title: Galactic Waltz NGC 1532-31
caption: The interacting galaxies NGC 1532 and NGC 1531, imaged by the Gemini South telescope

recognition.text: Official NSF NOIRLab / Gemini press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Two galaxies are locked together in what NOIRLab calls a fiery waltz. The larger, NGC 1532, is a spiral that we see nearly edge-on from our vantage point in the Milky Way. Intense reddish star-forming regions spatter the edges of its dusty arms, which stand out in silhouette in the foreground against the galaxy's disk.

Farther back, fainter spiral arms dimmed by intervening gas and dust reveal the galaxy's three-dimensional shape. The smaller partner, NGC 1531, is dwarfed by its companion, much as the Large Magellanic Cloud is dwarfed by the Milky Way.

The encounter has left clues, including at least two stray groupings of stars and red clumps of glowing hydrogen. A warp in one of NGC 1532's background arms, together with a possible bridge of matter linking the pair, suggests the two are still influencing each other. Astronomers estimate that NGC 1532 is slightly more massive than our own galaxy.

understand.summary: Taken with GMOS on Gemini South through U, g, r, i and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The hydrogen-alpha filter highlights glowing hydrogen in star-forming regions, and the long exposure gathers far more light than the eye.

explore: According to the caption, the pair sits roughly 55 million light-years away in the direction of Eridanus, in the southern sky. It belongs to a larger group, with at least one more dwarf galaxy lying beyond the edges of this frame. The image was made with Gemini South's Multi-Object Spectrograph (GMOS).
alt: A large, nearly edge-on spiral galaxy with dusty arms and reddish star-forming regions, beside a much smaller companion galaxy.
